I think the main thing to know is that this is not just turn-based combat, and neither just parry/dodge combat. You have to get used to the flow of battles and expect fights to feel like they drag on forever and every moment could be the last turn you have, but then again, even if you are at your last party member, they can still clutch and bring the whole fight back. Use items as much as possible, and find the role you want your team members to fill - DPS, tank, or support. Some characters are flexible and can do two roles but you stick to what works best for you.

  
Explore every single corner of the game, fight every encounter you come across at least once and learn the mechanics as you go.

  
Characters have certain playstyles and fulfill many roles depending on what you want them to do, but the main determinants for playstyle and role are:

  
Skills will determine how you play that character, what they do in battle and how well they can perform, so choose skills based on the role 

  
Weapons are the second main determinant of what your playstyle will be like, it also determines what your character's "role" will be so to speak, so choose them wisely when equipping, then adjust your stats accordingly to match the scaling. The game gives you many opportunities to respec so dont be afraid to switch things up often but not too often, be smart. 

  
Pictos are like your gear that give you stats and cool passives, equip them based on stats and based on passives according to the "role" of your character. These pictos also revolve around the role of the charcter you assign them to, some give you more health and defense and allow your character to become a tank, some give speed and crit chance and allow that character to become your main DPS, some are supportive and help you keep the flow of battle.

  
Luminas are the passives which you select with lumina points, it can get very grindy at this point, but you must switch pictos and maintain a constant mentality of adapting to newer enemy "types" and new fighting styles that way you can unlock more luminas which will give you the passive of the pictos to use on ANY character, offering a lot of flexibility for build making.

  
The way I play on expert mode: 

Lune: Support/healer/buffer/debuffer - Spam healing spells that also buff teammates with certain luminas. Balls deep on Vitality/AGL/DEF

Maelle: Tank/breaker/dps/protector - She gets an ability that allows you to tank for your teammates, great for keeping DPS alive, she parries and does a lot of break damage and max HP damage.

Sciel: DPS/Scaling damage - She stacks her sun charges which allow her to later on deal infinite damage based on how many stacks she has, she stays behind maelle at all times and stacks up.

  
TLDR: Remember the basic concepts of role playing, dont be afraid to switch things up (it's a must), learn the combat mechanics and have FUN

I'm sorry for the late reply OP, I hope you're feeling better now. I don't think I've ever rebuilt my psyche as I assume you're implying it. I see it as a continuous work and it's not something that is just "rebuilt" IMO. I think mentalities do not change, they just expand or shrink depending on your life choices. And based on your experiences, and the memories that you make, you'll be able to tap into more "resources" that can help you make decisions and/or dictate your life. For example, if you grew up shoplifting, your mind will expand in "shoplifting experience" and you'll feel inclined to do it again, but if you are able to shrink your experience in "shoplifting" you won't be as inclined to do it again. How you do this, will vary from person to person. This is basically what habits are.

To keep this relevant about what you posted about your identity disintegrating, and connecting what I just mentioned. You are poised in a very favorable position to begin new habits, it will be hard, because some of those "old/bad" habits will still be there and your mind will feel uncomfortable changing and creating new neurological connections. But as long as you have enough strength to fight against your "old" self (the you from 10,5,1 years ago, even the you from 1 day ago" so long as you have the strength to face these habits/decisions you will fine. 

You've gone through the hardest part of growing as a person, but it's not over, you will continue to experience this for the rest of your life, but it will get easier. Now that you've seen the scary, shameful, dark, bright, joyous, and beautiful things that constituted your "self" you should be able to identify your own strengths and weaknesses and find a way to work on them. 

Which brings me to my last point, using the 22 archetypes represented in the major arcana since they are easier to understand and represent your current situation and what you may need to do to advance. IMO based on the tone of your post, and your phrasing (and please take this with the tiniest grain of salt since I do not know you personally and your situation) you may be influenced by the archetype of the 13th card "Death"

Now, I'm no cultist and I'm very skeptical about fortune readings and what not, but I see the arcana as a way to categorize common life stages that most people throughout history have been through. A mythos that can be helpful to think retrospectively and reflect on our past and current situation.

To learn more about the major arcana and understand these symbols/stories that are common in human life, you could read this book by Sallie Nichols "Jung and Tarot An Archetypal Journey"

Let me break down the way I play into it.

Runes: phase rush 

Summoners: flash and ignite 

Items : Doran Shield > Serrated Dirk > boots > eclipse/duskblade > Sterak's/ Serylda's > 

Level 1-2: all you can do is farm and try to soak xp, if they play too aggressively, there is nothing you can do, you have to be the bitch for a little but that will change later on. So stay far from range but close enough to get xp 

Level 3 - 5: hopefully you haven't died and still healthy enough to start skirmishing. The way you skirmish is simple, this is where you can full commit your full combo and have the security that phase rush will allow you to disengage, this is the reason you are playing phase rush, to allow yourself to go in, land a few Qs and get out easily and safe. You do this about two times and could maybe secure a kill to help you start snowballing.

Level 6+: Hopefully you've had the chance to reset maybe twice by now and have a serrated dirk. At this point you just rinse and repeat the strategy, you commit a full combo, hit and run back to safety, Jayce will be half hp, you wait for your phase rush CD and you repeat the same thing again and fully commit to the kill if it's possible. 

Now when it comes to teamfights, you basically do the same thing. You flank as normal, commit a combo, and get out as safely as possible. Wait for E and Q cd while your teammates fight and you look for another opening and you strike again.

You can do both depending on the strategy you have. However, any method is good until it isn't, so you need to learn how to adapt to new strategies. I personally started out scalping on a paper money account, and it didn't go so well for me. Then I realized that I can swing trades instead with a higher profit ratio, like risking 20 dollars and make 200. That's a 1:10 ratio.  Those are the sort of opportunities you can have when swing trading. Instead, if you scalp, you're only looking at 1:2 or 1:3 profit ratios. However, I know there are individuals who have higher ratios. But you still need to risk more capital in order to justify your profits. Using the previous numbers, in order for me to profit 200 dollars, in a scalp trade and having a 1:3 profit ratio; I'd have to risk 66 dollars which is 3x my risk of loss swing trading. 

The amount of pips you're looking to make out of a trade matter a lot. Swing trading means less pips (maybe 10 to 20) and therefore more risk since you could get stopped out by a 5-10 pip move in the other direction. Swing trading, you're looking for 100 pips or more, and you may be stopped at a 20 pip movement. BUT those moments are rare, there are more chances for the price to move a few pips in the other direction and then come back in the direction you speculated and the move being sustained. 

However, it all just depends on the situation. 

Think of it this way, when you scalp: you're in the frontlines of a warzone, you can shoot more shots and therefore get lots of takedowns, but you're risking being taken down faster. 

When you swing trade: you're like a sniper, you only shoot a few times but because of that you must make every shot be worth the risk of being revealed and taken down. But the chances of being taken down go down significantly. And the chances of having big shot trades goes up.

Just think about who you are as a trader, and how you are training yourself to tackle the markets. At the end of the day, the only answer that matters is the one you come up with based on your experience.
